# dsh-hf-spaces

> A DeepSeek Harness plugin, alpha and not released on npm yet, that runs open-weight LLMs on the
> user's own GPU virtual machine on Hugging Face (a GPU Space) and uses them like any other model
> in the Harness. The Space starts when a message is sent, shows its start progress in the
> conversation header, and is paused when idle or at a time limit, so the GPU bills only while
> used. The user chooses the weights, including models with fewer refusals; the plugin adds no
> content filter, and its README sets the responsible-use terms. Credentials are referenced by
> name, never stored in configuration and never asked for in a chat. The user builds the Space
> (GPU hardware, OpenAI-compatible inference engine such as llama.cpp, weights, sleep time); the
> plugin starts, watches, uses and pauses it.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): the flow end to end, open models, responsible use, requirements (Hugging Face PRO plan), step-by-step installation with expected results and stop conditions, credentials, configuration, compatibility
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): mandatory rules for AI agents and contributors (no secrets, no personal data, English only, offline tests, no breakage on Harness updates, ready-to-use and deterministic setup)
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): architecture, Space lifecycle, configuration schema, progress protocol, interface, Hugging Face and Harness facts with dates
- [docs/contracts.md](docs/contracts.md): verified Hugging Face and Harness API contracts (responses, verification level, date); read before writing code that calls them

## For AI agents installing it

- Follow README.md, section "Installation", step by step; stop at the first step whose result does not match.
- Step 3 (the Hugging Face token) is the user's: never ask for a token in the chat and never write one yourself.
- Use only open models whose license allows the use, and refuse uses listed under "Responsible use".

## Reference

- [examples/config.example.yml](examples/config.example.yml): commented configuration with fake values
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): changes by version
